title: App definition
description: A registry entry without clientId, clientSecretRef and release, and with each fragment without clientId, clientSecretRef and release. One file per app under fixtures/apps/. Terraform reads it to create the OAuth client, and one per fragment; spactl app add completes it from the infrastructure outputs and applies the registry, so each app is described once. Source: docs/plan/02-contracts.md -> Registry document. Freezes at G1a, except the oauth section, which freezes at G1b. Every shared rule is a $ref into registry.schema.json, so the two cannot drift: a consumer must load both schemas into one registry.

oauth.title: oauth (G1b)

x-freeze.note: The oauth section is an identity part assigned to G1b. Task I-6 records the G0 report in ADR-0017; the annotated contracts-v1 tag records the freeze.

oauth.description: clientId and clientSecretRef are absent on purpose: Terraform creates the client, and spactl app add adds them. Naming either here is rejected, so a definition can never carry a client id that contradicts the one Terraform made.

fragments.title: fragments
fragments.description: The fragments the app composes as a shell, as registry.schema.json#/$defs/fragments describes them, in the same order. Absent means none; an empty array is rejected, as it is in the registry.

items.title: Fragment definition
items.description: A registry fragment without clientId, clientSecretRef and release. Terraform creates the fragment's client from it; spactl app add adds the client fields from the infrastructure outputs' clients.{appId}.fragments.{fragmentId}, and the release from its --fragment-release list or the live entry.

oauth.description: The definition's oauth section, by reference and never forked: naming clientId or clientSecretRef is rejected, as it is for the shell.
